cases.content: For this project, Nadia is the person who approves releases.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve Nadia as the current release approver; do not add an approval event.

cases.content: The launch checklist from April said Nadia approved releases. I am describing the April policy, not a current instruction.
cases.review_criterion: A supported historical memory preserves the April/checklist qualification; it must not assert that Nadia is the current approver.

cases.content: The earlier project note said that archival exports used Zstandard.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve an attributed historical report about Zstandard exports, without asserting the current export format.

cases.content: During Tuesday's handoff, Mira reported that the staging host uses port 4317. I have not checked it myself.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve attribution to Mira and the unverified nature of the report; do not present the port as independently confirmed.

cases.content: We used port 4317 for staging last year. That is no longer our staging port.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve the historical or explicitly obsolete status of port 4317; do not invent the replacement port.

cases.content: I stopped using Trello in March; that used to be my task tracker.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve discontinued use of Trello and the March qualifier; do not record a current preference for Trello.

cases.content: In a fictional example, a character named Nadia approves every release. This is not our project policy.
cases.review_criterion: Abstain from durable project or personal assertions about the fictional example.

cases.content: Did our earlier checklist actually say Nadia approved releases?
cases.review_criterion: Abstain; the question supplies no affirmative policy evidence.

cases.content: If we ever changed the export format, perhaps Zstandard would be worth considering.
cases.review_criterion: Abstain from asserting an adopted format or standing requirement.

cases.content: I think you would prefer Trello for task tracking.
cases.review_criterion: Abstain from asserting a user preference from the assistant suggestion.

cases.content: The next release must include signed exports. We have not built signing yet.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve the future requirement and incomplete status; do not assert that signed exports already exist.

cases.content: For release reviews I prefer a short written checklist before the meeting.
cases.review_criterion: Preserve a user preference for a short checklist before release-review meetings.

candidate_clause: A user may report a prior project state or what a named source said. Such a report can support a memory of that history or report even when it is not a current requirement. Preserve its attribution, time, uncertainty, negation, and obsolete status in the fact text; never turn it into an unqualified current fact or an instruction to act. Fiction, questions, hypotheticals, and assistant suggestions still do not establish user preferences or adopted project decisions.
interpretation: Development proposals only; no fact commits, retrieval, or lifecycle acceptance.
Manual review criteria frozen before calls; no automated semantic truth score.
Previously discovered failure class, not unseen heldout evaluation.
No selective retry, criteria revision, or production prompt change.
